title: Wide string in-place truncation
summary: Recovered VA 0x44fcf0 (63 bytes): unsigned length validation, capacity<8 inline selection, length publication, one UTF-16 NUL write, and return of this. GCC i386 thiscall models ECX and RET 4. Original caller 0x44fb63 uses this during self-substring assignment before prefix erasure. Invalid positions call nonreturning std::_Xout_of_range through IAT 0x92d16c with message at 0x99995c. The portable implementation delegates that dependency to a supplied nonreturning C hook.
test_description: Direct calls to original_wide_truncate and recovered_wide_truncate for every length and truncation position through inline capacities 0,1,7 and heap capacities 8,9,31,UINT_MAX with lengths 0..31. Whole fixture comparisons verify return identity, exact length/NUL writes, unchanged capacity, pointer, trailing characters, unused storage, and canaries. Recovered invalid length+1 and UINT_MAX cases use GCC builtin nonlocal transfer from a nonreturning error hook and check message and absence of writes. Local supplementary testing also intercepted the original error import at 0x92d16c using a private linker layout and passed; submitted portable tests skip invalid original calls because the trusted harness does not promise that import mapping. Local original reference was assembled at its original VA and compared to Game.exe.
known_limits: The original MSVC exception implementation, runtime type, and unwinding are not recovered. A Linux port must implement recovered_wide_out_of_range with its chosen faithful exception integration.

Submitted tests cannot execute the original rejection path without a mapped nonreturning CRT helper at IAT 0x92d16c; this external dependency is not an accepted reference routine. Local interception verifies dispatch and untouched state but not Windows exception unwinding.
Object layout and original ABI tests target 32-bit pointers; this is not a native 64-bit object-layout port. WideUnit deliberately remains 16 bits.

Malformed objects, invalid storage pointers, and oversized lengths that do not describe accessible storage are outside tested object invariants. No allocation or validation beyond the observed length check is added.
